m5: Liquidity. Volume measures the value traded on a market since it opened; liquidity (Polymarket) or open interest (Kalshi) measures what's available to buy or sell. A deeper market aggregates more opinions and reacts less to a single order. Below ${{thin}} of cumulative volume, a market is flagged as thin.

dek: L'Écart compares, daily, the implied probabilities of prediction markets with probabilities simulated from polls. The divergence between the two is the object of this monitoring exercise.

blackoutBody: French law (Act No. 77-808 of 19 July 1977) bars publishing election poll results the day before and the day of each round. Poll-simulated probabilities and market prices are hidden until this period ends. See the legal notice.
blackoutMeta: Publication suspended for the election-silence period (Act of 19 July 1977); data resumes once it ends.

h2a: Two readings of the same race
subA: Each row compares the market-implied probability against the probability simulated from polls: the mint marks give Polymarket's price then Kalshi's, never a mean; the black tick marks the polls. The gap is computed separately for each venue.
dvHint: No dated event is recorded for this period.
dvCap: Poll-simulated and market-implied probability of winning, by week.
dvSrc: Sources: polls from MieuxVoter/presidentielle2027; market prices from Polymarket and Kalshi, shown as data.
dvAria: Polls and market lines for {n}, with the gap between them
m1: Probability simulated from polls. Monte Carlo, 20,000 draws: each draw takes a random first-round poll, adds an error growing with score, and keeps the top two. The runoff comes from that pairing's head-to-head polls plus an error; untested pairings go by first-round strength. Every candidacy is assumed confirmed.
m2: Uncertainty applied. Polls can diverge sharply from the result months out: five months before the 2022 first round, they underestimated Jean-Luc Mélenchon by more than ten points. "Medium" applies an error of about 1.5 points plus 20% of the first-round score, 6 points at the runoff. The setting tests how sensitive the result is to that assumption.
m3: Market-implied probability. Two venues, shown separately, never averaged. Kalshi, a regulated US exchange, gives only the winner price. Polymarket, blocked in France by the ANJ since July 2026, also gives the runoff-qualification price. Where both price an event, the page shows both, or their range. Dated prices, shown as data, no link to either platform, academic use only.
m4: Sources. Polls are drawn from the open MieuxVoter/presidentielle2027 repository (MIT licence), compiled from surveys published under the supervision of the Commission des sondages. Each poll remains the property of its institute and sponsor.
aboutP1: L'Écart is an academic research project by Luke Segault, comparing the market-implied probability with the probability simulated from polls for the 2027 French presidential election, to measure their divergence and its possible causes.
aboutOnly: Academic research only: not a forecast, not advice, not an invitation to bet.
aboutContact: Contact: questions, corrections or data requests via GitHub.
